dissent.rationale: The underlying joint longitudinal measurement-error problem is real, but several assertions are too categorical. Prescribing, dispensing, and ingestion are distinct variables; their difference is misclassification only when the estimand targets one but the protocol measures another. In a cumulative inverse-probability weight, an erroneous treatment factor at time s remains in later cumulative products for a clone still at risk, but a clone artificially censored at s has no later weights. Mismeasurement of a time-varying confounder changes artificial-censoring membership only when that variable determines the dynamic strategy, eligibility, or censoring rule; under a static sustained strategy it can distort nuisance models without changing who is censored. The resulting biases can interact, but the defensible claim is that no unique identified additive measurement-versus-confounding decomposition generally exists without additional assumptions, not that no decomposition is possible. title: The visit process is treated as a nuisance to be imputed rather than as part of the causal structure
statement: Biomarkers and diagnoses are observed when a patient attends care and a clinician orders a test. That visit process depends on latent severity, on prior treatment and often on an impending outcome, so record-based covariate histories are irregular and selectively missing in a way that carries clinical information. Missing-at-random conditional on the recorded history can therefore fail precisely because the recording is itself informative. Standard handling, and last observation carried forward in particular, constructs an artificial history in which a patient's state is asserted to be unchanged over an interval during which the absence of measurement was itself evidence about their state.
why_open: Conditioning on having been observed can open a collider path, so the natural fix makes a different bias, and choosing between them requires knowing the structure that is in question. Inverse-intensity-of-visit weights are unstable when visit rates vary by an order of magnitude across patients, which they do. Modeling the visit process jointly with treatment and outcome multiplies the nuisance components and therefore the positivity requirements, so the more faithful model can be the less identifiable one.

proposed_direction: Model visits as recurrent events or point processes jointly with treatment and outcome, and compare complete case, last observation carried forward, multiple imputation, inverse-intensity weighting and joint latent-state targeted learning on data generated with a known, treatment-dependent visiting mechanism. Include healthcare use as a process in the causal diagram rather than as a baseline confounder, so that conditioning decisions can be read off the graph. Report visit-weight dispersion and the calibration of the predicted visit intensity, since an uncalibrated intensity model produces weights that look like adjustment and are noise.
severity: It affects every time-varying covariate in every record-based emulation and the default handling is known to be wrong.

opinions.rationale: The central problem is technically real. When visit or test ordering depends on treatment and on an unobserved current prognostic state, missingness need not be at random given recorded history; LOCF then replaces an unknown trajectory with a constant one. Identification remains open without additional structural assumptions, external measurements, or sensitivity parameters. Several supporting claims are too broad. Conditioning on observation opens a collider path only under particular causal structures. Inverse-intensity weights require conditional independent observation, correct intensity models, and observation positivity; heterogeneity in marginal visit rates, even by an order of magnitude, does not by itself make the weights unstable. Joint modeling adds nuisance models and identifying assumptions, but it does not automatically multiply positivity requirements. Calibration is useful but insufficient because a conditionally misspecified intensity model can be marginally calibrated. Very high severity is proportionate only when decision-relevant eligibility variables, confounders, or outcomes are materially visit-dependent, not for every record-based emulation.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: In record-based emulations where visiting or testing depends on prior treatment and on current prognostic state not captured in recorded history, MAR given recorded history can fail, LOCF can distort time-varying covariate histories, and conditioning on observation can induce selection bias under the relevant causal structures. Inverse-intensity weighting can address conditionally independent visiting when the intensity model is correct and observation positivity holds; latent-state-dependent visiting requires additional identifying assumptions or sensitivity analysis. Weight instability is driven by small conditional observation probabilities or intensities and model misspecification, not marginal visit-rate heterogeneity alone, and calibration alone does not validate an intensity model.

opinions.rationale:
Inverted-prior search finds methods that put the visit process in the causal or estimating structure, so the problem is not open as a pure absence of methodology. It is not fully solved either: the report’s hard tradeoffs remain live, and the comparative evaluation it proposes has not been delivered for sustained-strategy target trial emulation under a known, treatment-dependent visiting mechanism.

Cited works first. Goldstein et al. (JAMIA 2019; 10.1093/jamia/ocz148) characterize when informative visits bias EHR association analyses; that paper diagnoses the mechanism and does not close it. Wang et al. (npj Digit Med 2026; 10.1038/s41746-026-02563-z) elevate the observation process to an operational constraint on whether an EHR can realize a target trial protocol element. Secondary commentary on that paper treats the contribution as specification-versus-realization discipline, not as a solved estimator. Both strengthen the claim that the issue is still on the agenda; neither resolves identification or estimation under treatment-dependent visiting.

Prior art that treats visits as structure rather than pure nuisance: (i) inverse-intensity-of-visit (IIW) theory and software for irregular longitudinal data (Pullenayegum line; CRAN IrregLong with Cox visit-intensity weights and IIW-GEE), still actively refined in 2025 on visit-model variable selection and selection of patients with no follow-up; (ii) parametric g-formula software that models a random measurement or visit process jointly with covariates for sustained strategies (gfoRmula’s visitprocess argument: visit indicators attached to intermittently measured confounders, with last-measured values and a cap on consecutive missed visits); (iii) Kalia et al. (BMC Med Res Methodol 2023; 10.1186/s12874-022-01831-2), calibrated inverse probability weights for marginal structural models under irregular visits, with Monte Carlo evaluation; (iv) Kalia et al. (Stat Med 2025; 10.1002/sim.70102), continuous-time MSM weights factored as visit intensity times dose (marked point process) on primary-care EHR for cumulative SGLT-2i exposure and recurrent UTI, explicitly motivated by informative visit timing. Coulombe et al. (Stat Methods Med Res 2023) combine inverse intensity of visit weights with individualized treatment rules in longitudinal observational data, which is related but not full sustained-strategy TTE.

What remains open, and why a full solved vote fails. IIW and continuous-time visit weights still require sequential positivity for the visit intensity and can be unstable when intensities vary sharply across patients; Kalia 2025 itself discusses extreme weights, stabilization, and constrained optimal weights, not elimination of the variance problem the report flags. Joint visit–treatment–outcome models still multiply nuisance components and positivity requirements; that structural cost is not removed by packaging. gfoRmula’s visit process assumes a discrete grid and a correctly specified visit model, and still encodes non-visit intervals via last measured values, so it does not by itself refute the LOCF critique for continuous-time EHR generation. No 2024–2026 paper or package release was found that runs the report’s proposed horse race (complete case, LOCF, MI, IIW, joint latent-state targeted learning) on data generated with a known treatment-dependent visiting mechanism in a sustained-strategy TTE design. Method proposals and single-setting applications therefore count as partial, not full, resolution.

Package and guidance scan. IrregLong and gfoRmula implement visit or measurement process handling; TrialEmulation, lmtp, ltmle, WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt, ipw, adjustedCurves, riskRegression, zEpid, causallib, lifelines, and scikit-survival did not surface merged work that closes this gap for informative EHR visit processes under sustained strategies. 2025–2026 RWE guidances (FDA RWE, EMA/HMA registry, ICH E9(R1), TARGET, HARPER/STaRT-RWE, ENCePP, ISPE, NICE) frame data-generation and missingness issues at a high level; none was found that settles a preferred causal handling of informative visits for TTE.

Caveat on the claim as stated. Applied TTE and EHR pipelines still often grid time and carry forward or impute under MAR, so the nuisance framing is still a fair description of common practice. The methodological literature has long refused that framing, so a reader who only knows IIW, gfoRmula visitprocess, or continuous-time marked point process MSMs would find the absolute statement overstated. The agenda item that remains is comparative, practical, and identification-theoretic under realistic visit heterogeneity, not the invention of the first joint visit model.

title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption
statement: Death, treatment discontinuation and competing clinical events change what an outcome contrast means. ICH E9(R1) requires that intercurrent events be handled explicitly, and the causal competing-risks literature distinguishes total effects, controlled direct effects and separable effects, each answering a different question. Applied emulations nonetheless default to cause-specific hazards or censor competing events without matching the estimator to the causal question, and recurrent and terminal events are seldom modeled jointly. The step where an analyst censors follow-up at death is an identifying decision that selects among these estimands, and it is normally executed silently inside data preparation, where no reviewer sees it as a decision at all.
why_open: The estimands differ in what they assume rather than in what they fit, so a wrong choice produces a well-behaved analysis of the wrong quantity and nothing downstream flags it. Separable effects require decomposing a treatment into components whose separate effects are meaningful, which is a substantive claim about the drug that most applied settings cannot support. Recurrent-event and terminal-event models are available but their combination with sustained-strategy emulation is not worked out, so the analyst choosing correctly on competing risks may have no estimator for the regime they wanted.

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
statement: A deterministic treatment strategy can assign a treatment that clinicians almost never give to patients with certain covariate histories. The standard response is to inspect the weight distribution and truncate the tail, which reduces variance, changes the implicit estimand and can leave substantial bias in place. What the diagnostic does not report is the quantity a reader needs: what fraction of the target population has no support for the strategy under study, which histories are the unsupported ones, and what estimand remains identified once they are set aside. A 2026 study of non-mutually exclusive assignment found that poor overlap defeated adjustment methods that were otherwise well specified, which is the failure mode a weight histogram is least able to show.
why_open: Practical positivity is a property of a conditional density over a growing history, so with more than a handful of time points the object to be diagnosed is high-dimensional and cannot be plotted. Truncation is attractive precisely because it converts an identification failure into a variance reduction, which reads as a modelling improvement rather than as a change of question. There is also no agreed target: reporting the unsupported fraction requires deciding what counts as support, and any threshold is a decision about the estimand that nobody currently has to state.

prior_work.what_it_does: Shows that poor overlap can defeat advanced adjustment methods, in a setting where assignment to strategies is not mutually exclusive.

prior_work.what_it_does: Implements modified treatment policies and stochastic interventions for binary, categorical, continuous and multivariate treatments with censored outcomes and competing risks, which is the estimand class that restores positivity.

proposed_direction: Replace deterministic interventions that the data cannot support with modified treatment policies, incremental propensity-score interventions or stochastic initiation rules, and state the trade in the paper rather than in the weight truncation. Report a causal support map over patient histories: the fraction of the target population with adequate support, which histories fail, and the estimand that survives. Derive partial-identification bounds for the unsupported strata, and set overlap-aware eligibility criteria before any outcome analysis so that restricting the population is a design decision with a date rather than a result.
severity: A precise estimate produced by extrapolation into regions with no data is not evidence, and nothing in the standard report distinguishes it from one that is.

opinions.rationale: The entry's core claim, that diagnostics describe weights rather than naming which histories are unsupported, holds against the corpus. Two pieces of work sharpen rather than resolve it. A 2025 study measures the impact of near-positivity violations on IPTW-estimated marginal structural survival models with time-dependent covariates, which supplies the consequence the entry asserts. A 2026 American Journal of Epidemiology paper on target trial emulation under non-mutually exclusive assignment sets out structural pitfalls and remedies for exactly the overlap failure the entry cites. Neither produces a causal support map over histories, an unsupported-fraction statistic, or partial-identification bounds for the unsupported strata, so the specific artifacts the entry says are missing are still missing.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Positivity is diagnosed through weight distributions rather than through a statement of what fraction of the target population is unsupported and which treatment histories fail, and no partial-identification bound is routinely reported for the unsupported strata.

resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Measures how near-positivity degrades weighted longitudinal survival estimation, supporting the entry's premise that truncation does not rescue the estimate.

opinions.rationale: A marginal weight histogram cannot localize poor support to particular histories, and structural nonpositivity is a decision-grade identification failure. However, the report conflates structural nonpositivity, practical near-nonpositivity, and finite-sample instability. Weight truncation does not convert an identification failure into variance reduction or necessarily define a coherent alternative causal estimand. It changes the estimating functional and usually biases estimation of the stated target, while structural nonpositivity remains unidentified. The claim that the high-dimensional object cannot be plotted is also too absolute because reduced history-specific diagnostics are possible. Pinned CICI 1.0 is a direct partial counterexample: its NAMESPACE exports feasible, plot.feasible, and summary.feasible; feasible() estimates conditional treatment densities, returns per-observation feasible intervention values and low_matrix objects, and reports the proportion below its threshold by strategy and time. Its gformula accepts the resulting individual intervention matrices. This implementation is limited to continuous interventions and an analyst-chosen alpha threshold, does not provide general partial-identification bounds, and does not cover arbitrary binary or categorical sustained strategies. Its threshold implementation also normalizes densities using bin widths but calculates cumsum(sort(row)) without bin-width weighting, so the advertised probability-mass threshold is miscalibrated whenever bin widths differ from one. Later-time diagnostics are evaluated over observed histories, which need not equal the history distribution induced by the intervention. Pinned lmtp 1.5.4 implements longitudinal modified treatment policies and an ipsi policy factory, but such intervention classes do not automatically restore positivity; policy-specific absolute continuity remains necessary, and lmtp trims estimated density ratios by default. Very-high severity is warranted when the prespecified strategy materially lacks support, but a universal support map and bounds are roadmap extensions rather than requirements for every adequately supported analysis.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Marginal weight summaries do not identify which intervention-relevant histories have small or zero treatment density. Analysts should prespecify a policy-specific support criterion, report time- and history-localized diagnostics and sensitivity to that criterion, and replace or restrict unsupported deterministic regimes when scientifically acceptable. Weight truncation is only bias-variance regularization and cannot identify effects under structural nonpositivity. Existing software partly addresses this for continuous longitudinal interventions, but a validated general solution for arbitrary sustained strategies and partial-identification bounds remains open.

This resolves the central diagnostic request for a limited continuous-treatment setting.

opinions.rationale:
Inverted prior: treat the diagnostic gap as already closed, then check. The report's own citations do not close it. Takayama (AJE 2026; 10.1093/aje/kwaf018) shows that poor overlap can defeat well-specified adjustment under non-mutually exclusive assignment; that is evidence the failure mode is real, not a fix for naming unsupported histories. lmtp implements modified treatment policies (MTPs) and stochastic interventions that can restore positivity by changing the estimand; that is the estimand-class response the agenda already proposes, not a diagnostic that reports which histories lack support or what fraction of the target population is unsupported.

What does close most of the stated gap is recent prior art the agenda does not cite. Danelian et al. (Journal of Causal Inference 2023; 10.1515/jci-2022-0032) introduced PoRT, a regression-tree diagnostic that flags in-sample positivity violations as interpretable covariate-defined subgroups, with implementation in the CRAN package RISCA (`port`). dissent.rationale: A marginal weight histogram cannot localize poor support to particular histories, and structural nonpositivity is a decision-grade identification failure. However, the report conflates structural nonpositivity, practical near-nonpositivity, and finite-sample instability. Weight truncation does not convert an identification failure into variance reduction or necessarily define a coherent alternative causal estimand. It changes the estimating functional and usually biases estimation of the stated target, while structural nonpositivity remains unidentified. The claim that the high-dimensional object cannot be plotted is also too absolute because reduced history-specific diagnostics are possible. Pinned CICI 1.0 is a direct partial counterexample: its NAMESPACE exports feasible, plot.feasible, and summary.feasible; feasible() estimates conditional treatment densities, returns per-observation feasible intervention values and low_matrix objects, and reports the proportion below its threshold by strategy and time. Its gformula accepts the resulting individual intervention matrices. This implementation is limited to continuous interventions and an analyst-chosen alpha threshold, does not provide general partial-identification bounds, and does not cover arbitrary binary or categorical sustained strategies. Its threshold implementation also normalizes densities using bin widths but calculates cumsum(sort(row)) without bin-width weighting, so the advertised probability-mass threshold is miscalibrated whenever bin widths differ from one. Later-time diagnostics are evaluated over observed histories, which need not equal the history distribution induced by the intervention. Pinned lmtp 1.5.4 implements longitudinal modified treatment policies and an ipsi policy factory, but such intervention classes do not automatically restore positivity; policy-specific absolute continuity remains necessary, and lmtp trims estimated density ratios by default. Very-high severity is warranted when the prespecified strategy materially lacks support, but a universal support map and bounds are roadmap extensions rather than requirements for every adequately supported analysis.

title: No decomposition separates scientific-target mismatch from protocol compromise, mapping loss and estimation error
statement: Three trials are in play in any emulation and only one of them is usually named. There is the ideal trial that would answer the decision-maker's question, the target trial that the investigator specifies, and the emulation the data actually support. Specifying the target trial closely around the available data conceals the distance between the first two, and the paper reports a single estimate as though the chain were tight. What does not exist is a decomposition of the total discrepancy into its four transitions: from the ideal estimand to the feasible target estimand, from that to the identified observed-data functional, and from that to the estimator's output. Without one, a reader cannot tell whether a surprising result reflects estimation error or the fact that the question quietly changed at the first step.
why_open: The first transition is a change of scientific question rather than a statistical error, so it has no sampling distribution and no obvious metric. Any measure of distance between estimands requires a common space in which to compare an intervention that was never implementable with one that was, and that space has to be constructed rather than estimated. The incentives also run the wrong way: making the drift explicit weakens the paper's claim without changing its number, so nothing but a reporting requirement would make anyone do it.

prior_work.cite: Moreno-Betancur M, et al. The ideal trial: defining causal estimands that balance relevance and feasibility in target trial emulations and actual randomized trials. arXiv 2024
prior_work.what_it_does: Distinguishes ideal, target and actual trials and argues that every discrepancy between them should be made explicit. It frames the problem and does not supply the decomposition.

prior_work.cite: Hernán MA, Robins JM. Using big data to emulate a target trial when a randomized trial is not available. Am J Epidemiol 2016;183(8):758-764
prior_work.what_it_does: Establishes the target trial as the object to be specified, which is the middle term of the three and the only one the framework requires be written down.

prior_work.cite: Hansford HJ, et al. Design and implementation of observational studies emulating a target trial. JAMA Netw Open 2026
prior_work.what_it_does: Design guidance for the operational steps, acknowledging that the operational methods remain scenario dependent.

proposed_direction: Define an estimand lineage that records each transition as a formal change in population, treatment version, outcome definition or follow-up, and require it in the protocol so it is written before the estimate exists. Quantify estimand distance through differences in intervention support and in target-population composition, which are computable from the data at hand and do not require the ideal trial to be feasible. Report the lineage next to the estimate so a reader can see which step is carrying the assumption load.
severity: A paper can be internally valid and answer a question nobody asked, and nothing in the current report distinguishes the two.

opinions.rationale: The framing is now published rather than a preprint: the ideal-trial paper the entry cites as arXiv 2405.10026 appeared in Epidemiology in 2026, and the entry should cite the journal version. A 2026 American Journal of Epidemiology paper sets out the anatomy of a causal estimand for population health research, which is the vocabulary a lineage would be written in. Neither supplies the decomposition the entry asks for: a formal accounting that attributes total discrepancy across the four transitions, with a computable measure of estimand distance. The claim survives with its citation corrected and its neighbors named.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: The distinction between ideal, target and emulated trials is established and published; no decomposition attributes a study's total discrepancy across scientific-target mismatch, protocol compromise, observational mapping and estimation, and no computable measure of estimand distance is in use.

resolving_work.title: Clarifying causal questions in population health research: anatomy of a causal estimand
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Decomposes a causal estimand into its parts, which is the representation an estimand lineage would build on.

opinions.rationale: A structured estimand lineage is a defensible reporting objective, but the proposed decomposition is not mathematically defined. The statement names four objects but enumerates only three transitions. Under valid identification, the observed-data functional equals the target causal estimand and is not a separate loss term. If identification assumptions fail, the resulting causal bias is generally not identified from the same data. Effects defined using different populations, interventions, outcomes, or scales also have no canonical additive distance. Differences in intervention support or population composition neither decompose nor necessarily bound the difference between effects without bridge and effect-heterogeneity assumptions. This is therefore an open reporting and formalization item, not a universally available decomposition whose absence prevents interpretation, and its asserted high severity is inflated.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Emulations should separately document changes from the decision question to the operational causal estimand, the assumptions mapping that estimand to an observed-data functional, and estimation uncertainty. This lineage need not form an additive numerical decomposition when populations, interventions, outcomes, or scales differ.

opinions.rationale: Inverted prior: searched for a formal four-step discrepancy decomposition (ideal→target→identified functional→estimator) in TTE. Own prior_work (Moreno-Betancur arXiv:2405.10026) frames ideal/target/actual trials and urges explicit discrepancies but does not supply a quantitative decomposition of total discrepancy into scientific-target mismatch, mapping loss, and estimation error. Hernán–Robins 2016 and Hansford 2026 are design/guidance, not decomposition. Searches for estimand lineage, estimand distance, and four-transition decomposition in AJE/Epidemiology/IJE/Sim/BMJ/JAMA and arXiv 2024–2026 returned framing and reporting proposals (ICH E9(R1), TARGET) but no operational metric or software that separates those four transitions. Still open as stated.

The claim asserts that a decomposition 'does not exist,' which wears the language of impossibility. However, the reason given for it being open notes that the common space required for comparison 'has to be constructed rather than estimated,' implying that the decomposition is structurally possible but simply has not been developed or standardized in current practice. The claim is thus a statement about the current state of the field framed as an absolute.

title: Registrations record the final protocol and not the alternatives that were rejected
statement: An emulation makes many defensible decisions: active comparator, washout period, time zero, grace period, how treatment episodes are constructed, censoring rules, follow-up length and outcome definition. Each has more than one reasonable answer, and the set of answers is the researcher's degrees of freedom. Design guidance now exists and states plainly that the operational methods remain scenario dependent, which means the guidance narrows the set without closing it. Registrations, where they exist, record only the specification that was finally run; they do not record the alternatives considered, the order in which decisions were made, or which decisions were revised after the data were inspected. A reader therefore cannot distinguish a protocol written once from one converged upon.
why_open: The information that would settle it is destroyed rather than merely unrecorded: once a decision log is not kept, no later audit can reconstruct it, and there is no artifact to demand. Registration systems were designed for randomized trials, where the protocol precedes the data, and have no natural slot for a design that is necessarily developed against an existing dataset. Requiring a full multiverse imposes a cost proportional to the number of decisions, which for a longitudinal emulation is large, so the honest practice is also the expensive one.

proposed_direction: Require version-controlled protocols, dated decision logs and outcome-blinded feasibility reports, so that the chronology of decisions is an artifact rather than a memory. Prespecify a primary emulation plus a principled design multiverse over the decisions known to move estimates, and report the distribution rather than the chosen point. Hash the executable specification before outcome analysis, which makes the claim of prespecification checkable by a third party instead of taken on trust.
severity: Without the chronology, a reader cannot tell prespecification from post hoc convergence, and both look identical on the page.

title: An unobservable protocol component produces a different, data-defined estimand rather than a noisy version of the intended one
statement: The canonical protocol has seven linked components: eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcomes, causal contrast and analysis plan. Conceptual specification and operational realization are distinct, and when a required component cannot be observed the analyst does not obtain a mismeasured version of the intended effect. They obtain a different effect, defined by what the data can express. A criterion that cannot be verified is dropped and the population changes; a strategy that cannot be distinguished from its neighbor is merged and the contrast changes; an outcome that is only partly captured redefines the endpoint. Nothing in current reporting requires that substitution to be named, so the paper states the intended estimand and reports the substituted one.
why_open: The substitution happens component by component during implementation, often in code rather than in prose, and by the time results exist there is no artifact recording which component was compromised. Naming the substituted estimand requires a language for partially specified interventions that does not yet exist in a usable form. There is also a reasonable disagreement underneath: some substitutions are innocuous refinements and others change the question, and no criterion separates them.

opinions.rationale: The statement treats all failures of observation as estimand substitution, which is incorrect. Depending on the measurement and identification structure, an operational proxy may still identify the intended effect through a valid measurement-error, missing-data, or validation model; it may define a different, well-defined causal effect; or it may identify only a statistical functional with no coherent intervention-based interpretation. Dropping an eligibility criterion, merging strategies, and redefining an endpoint change the target only when the analyst actually makes those substitutions. They are not logically forced by partial observation. Conversely, simply naming a substituted estimand does not make it causal or identified. Agreement with a benchmark trial cannot determine whether an estimand was preserved because different targets and compensating biases can yield similar estimates. Component-level conceptual-to-operational mapping is important and can be decision-critical, but the universal claim and very-high-severity framing are excessive.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: When an intended protocol variable is replaced by an operational proxy and no valid measurement, missing-data, or validation model recovers the intended variable, the resulting observed-data functional generally need not identify the intended causal effect. Analysts should state the operational target and assumptions, and should not label it a substituted causal estimand without a corresponding intervention and identification argument.

title: Emulation is proposed for non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions whose treatment versions and assignment units are not defined
statement: Interference, combination therapies, multiple treatment versions and non-pharmaceutical interventions all violate the two-arm, individually assigned, well-defined-intervention assumptions that the standard emulation protocol makes. Non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions are the sharpest case: the intervention is delivered to a place or an organization rather than a person, its content varies by implementer, its timing is gradual rather than dated, and there is often no version of not receiving it that is comparable. Emulation is nonetheless being applied to such questions, with the protocol components filled in by analogy. What is missing is a statement of which protocol components a policy intervention can actually satisfy and what estimand results when several cannot.
why_open: A well-defined intervention is a requirement of the causal framework and not of the emulation framework specifically, so this is inherited rather than introduced, and the emulation literature has no special claim on solving it. The assignment unit for a policy is usually a jurisdiction, which reduces the effective sample to the number of jurisdictions and makes the analysis a small-n problem regardless of how many patients it contains. Version variation is intrinsic to implementation rather than incidental, so the consistency assumption fails by construction rather than by accident.

prior_work.cite: Papadogeorgou G, Mealli F, Zigler CM. Causal inference with interfering units for cluster and population level treatment allocation programs. Biometrics 2019;75(3):778-787
prior_work.what_it_does: Provides the estimand framework for cluster and population-level allocation, which is the setting a policy emulation is in whether or not it says so.

prior_work.cite: Hernán MA, Robins JM. Using big data to emulate a target trial when a randomized trial is not available. Am J Epidemiol 2016;183(8):758-764
prior_work.what_it_does: States the well-defined-intervention requirement that policy questions strain, and the protocol components a policy emulation has to fill.

proposed_direction: Write protocol templates for cluster and policy target trials in which the assignment unit, the exposure mapping and the treatment-version class are explicit components rather than assumed, and state which components a given policy question can satisfy. Where versions cannot be unified, define the estimand over the observed distribution of versions and say so, rather than naming an intervention that no jurisdiction implemented. Establish minimum unit counts for credible inference at the jurisdiction level, since a study with millions of patients and eleven jurisdictions has eleven units of assignment.
severity: Policy emulations are published with individual-level precision and jurisdiction-level information.

resolving_work.title: Methodological innovations to advance substance use disorder research: proceedings of a NIDA workshop on target trial emulation
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Addresses emulation in a service and policy setting where the intervention is delivered at more than the individual level.

opinions.rationale: Target trial emulation is not intrinsically restricted to two arms or individual assignment. Combination therapies can be defined as multicomponent strategies; policies can be assigned at cluster level; and interference can be handled through explicit exposure mappings and cluster or population-level estimands. Multiple versions do not make consistency fail by construction when versions are specified, shown irrelevant, or incorporated into a well-defined stochastic intervention. The defect arises when a vague treatment label, assignment unit, version rule, timing, or interference structure is left unspecified. Cluster-level treatment variation makes the number and adoption patterns of independent clusters central to precision, but the effective sample size is not literally always the number of jurisdictions, and no universal minimum count is defensible without the design, dependence structure, and inferential method. Averaging over an observed version distribution is causal only after that stochastic intervention and its identification assumptions are defined. The cited cluster-allocation framework already resolves the alleged absence of an estimand framework, while standardized emulation protocols and finite-cluster guidance remain open.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Policy emulations require explicit specification of the assignment unit, timing, comparator, intervention versions or stochastic version rule, exposure mapping under interference, and cluster-level estimand. When treatment varies only across jurisdictions, independent jurisdictions and adoption variation, rather than patient count alone, dominate causal information.

title: Regulators have no thresholds for adequate emulation, acceptable residual confounding or sufficient sensitivity analysis
statement: FDA guidance asks sponsors to describe an approach that supports causal inference and names target trial emulation where appropriate. NICE states that some target trials cannot be adequately emulated and that bespoke data collection may then be preferable. EMA and ICH guidance emphasize fit-for-use data, prespecification and transparent non-interventional design. What none of them supplies is a threshold: how close an emulation must be to count as adequate, how much residual confounding is acceptable for a given decision, or what set of sensitivity analyses is sufficient. Sponsors therefore cannot know in advance whether a submission will be accepted, and reviewers have no consistent basis on which to accept or reject one.
why_open: A threshold requires a metric, and the quantities that matter, residual confounding and estimand distance, are not identified from the data of the study in question. Any fixed threshold would be gamed and would also be wrong for some decisions, since the tolerable bias depends on what the decision costs. Agencies are also reasoning from a small and non-random set of precedents, so the empirical base for calibrating a threshold does not yet exist.

prior_work.what_it_does: Asks sponsors to describe an approach supporting causal inference, naming target trial emulation where appropriate, without setting an acceptance threshold.

prior_work.cite: NICE real-world evidence framework
prior_work.what_it_does: Recognizes that some target trials cannot be adequately emulated and may require bespoke data collection, which is the closest any guidance comes to a stop rule.

prior_work.what_it_does: Establishes the estimand framework and the requirement for aligned sensitivity analyses, which regulators apply to trials and have not translated into thresholds for emulations.

proposed_direction: Build regulator-facing evidence dossiers that separate protocol fidelity, identification assumptions, data validation, diagnostics and decision uncertainty into distinct sections, so a reviewer can accept some and reject others rather than judging the whole. Conduct prospective qualification studies of data sources and phenotypes, in which fitness is established before the question is asked, rather than relying on post hoc reassurance. Use benchmarking evidence to calibrate what degree of protocol match has historically corresponded to what agreement, which is the only empirical route to a defensible threshold.
severity: The acceptance boundary is where emulation either enters decision-making or does not, and it is currently undefined on both sides.

A 2026 Journal of Clinical Oncology paper addresses emulation for regulatory and clinical decision making in cancer without setting an acceptance criterion. resolving_work.title: Target trial emulation for regulatory and clinical decision making in cancer
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Addresses the decision-facing use of emulation directly, and describes considerations rather than acceptance thresholds.

opinions.rationale: The absence of a universal numerical threshold is not an unresolved statistical defect. Residual confounding is generally unidentified without additional information, and acceptable bias depends on the estimand, decision loss, and uncertainty. Nevertheless, lacking a universal cutoff does not leave reviewers without a principled basis, and trial benchmarking cannot uniquely validate an emulation because agreement may reflect estimand differences, sampling error, or offsetting biases. Decision-specific tolerances, quantitative bias analysis, data validation, and prespecified diagnostics provide other bases for assessment.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Universal numerical cutoffs for emulation adequacy, residual confounding, and sensitivity-analysis sufficiency are not technically defensible. Regulators can instead apply prespecified, decision-specific criteria based on protocol fidelity, identification plausibility, data fitness, diagnostics, quantitative bias analysis, and decision robustness; randomized-trial benchmarking is supporting evidence rather than the only route to evaluation.

opinions.rationale: Inverted-prior search for regulatory acceptance thresholds on emulation adequacy, residual confounding, or sufficient sensitivity analysis did not find any. The problem’s own cited instruments still describe process and design expectations without numeric or decision-rule cutoffs. FDA July 2024 final guidance on EHR and claims data (and related non-interventional RWE guidance) recommends quantitative bias analysis for misclassification and reliability issues, fitness-for-use assessment, and transparent causal design including target trial emulation where appropriate, but does not state how close an emulation must be, how large residual confounding may be, or which sensitivity package is enough for acceptance. NICE’s RWE framework explicitly treats some target trials as not adequately emulable and prefers bespoke collection in those cases; secondary commentary on the final framework notes that NICE deliberately does not set minimum acceptable quality standards. EMA’s March 2025 reflection paper on RWD in non-interventional studies for regulatory purposes (EMA/99865/2025) endorses target trial emulation for causal objectives, ICH E9(R1)-aligned sensitivity analysis, and case-by-case relevance determination; it does not supply thresholds. ICH E9(R1) remains a trial estimand and sensitivity framework, not a translation into emulation acceptance rules. Adjacent methods work (E-values, tipping-point and quantitative bias analysis, Faries et al. 2025 good practices for robustness of observational evidence) equip sponsors to quantify bias under assumed parameters; that is not a regulator-issued decision threshold, and any fixed numeric bar would still be decision-dependent as the report states. No 2024–2026 FDA, EMA, HMA, ICH, NICE, Health Canada, CDA-AMC, or ENCePP instrument located here closes the gap. Queries included: FDA/NICE/EMA residual confounding threshold and acceptance criteria; quantitative bias analysis regulatory threshold; ICH E9(R1) observational thresholds; ENCePP/DARWIN acceptance criteria 2025–2026; plus review of the three cited guidance PDFs and the 2025 EMA reflection paper.

The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. title: There is no assumption dashboard, so diagnosable and undiagnosable assumptions are reported alike
statement: Exchangeability and consistency cannot be established from the observed data. Positivity, model behavior, balance and measurement validity can at least be diagnosed. Current reports blur the distinction: a propensity-score overlap plot is offered, and the reader is left to infer that the assumptions have been checked, when the plot bears on one of them and is silent on the rest. No standard set of diagnostics exists for an emulation, so what appears varies by author and by journal, and the absence of a diagnostic cannot be distinguished from a diagnostic that was run and not reported.
why_open: A dashboard is a convention rather than a discovery, and conventions require an adopting body. Several of the components are not yet standardized as measurements, since balance at each time, support by history and phenotype validity have no agreed summary statistic in the longitudinal setting. Separating the testable from the untestable also makes the untestable ones conspicuous, which is uncomfortable and is exactly the point.

prior_work.what_it_does: Establishes what must be reported about the protocol and its emulation, and is explicitly not a risk-of-bias or diagnostic standard.

proposed_direction: Define an assumption dashboard reporting covariate balance at each time, effective sample size, weight tails, support by treatment history, censoring rates, missingness, phenotype validity and sensitivity contours, arranged so that the empirically testable diagnostics are visibly separated from the untestable assumptions. Standardize a summary statistic for longitudinal balance and for support by history, since those are the two components that currently have no agreed form. Pair the dashboard with the reporting checklist so that a missing panel is a visible omission rather than an inference.
severity: Readers cannot currently tell a checked assumption from an unchecked one.

opinions.rationale: A standardized reporting convention remains a legitimate open implementation issue, but the proposed testable versus untestable division is too coarse. Observed data cannot establish exchangeability or consistency. Empirical positivity problems, nuisance-model behavior, and measured-covariate balance can be investigated, but finite-sample diagnostics cannot establish population positivity or model correctness. Measurement validity normally requires labeled, replicated, or external validation data, and balance is a property of the fitted analysis rather than a causal assumption. A dashboard would improve transparency but would not certify identification, so this is a reporting roadmap item rather than a solution to a decision-critical methodological gap.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Reports should explicitly separate causal assumptions that observed data cannot establish from partial diagnostics of empirical support, nuisance-model performance, measured-covariate balance, weighting, censoring, missingness, and measurement validity. These diagnostics can reveal or falsify particular problems but cannot certify exchangeability, consistency, positivity, model correctness, or phenotype validity, and no single longitudinal summary is adequate for every design.

opinions.rationale: No adopted, author-facing assumption dashboard that separates diagnosable diagnostics from undiagnosable identifying assumptions for target trial emulations was found. TARGET (Hansford/Cashin et al., JAMA 2025; also BMJ co-publication) is a 21-item reporting guideline for observational studies that explicitly emulate a target trial: it requires statement of the target protocol, mapping to data, identifying assumptions, and sensitivity analyses. It is deliberately not a risk-of-bias tool and not a standardized diagnostic panel; its own positioning matches the report’s prior-work note. Hansford et al. JAMA Netw Open 2023 documents uneven reporting of emulation components, which is baseline practice, not a dashboard. ROBINS-I and ROBINS-I V2 (launch materials 2024) structure reviewer risk-of-bias judgments relative to a specified target trial; that is systematic-review assessment, not a publication convention that forces authors to display balance over time, weight tails, effective sample size, support by treatment history, phenotype validity, and sensitivity contours in a fixed layout with testable panels visually separated from exchangeability and consistency. STaRT-RWE and HARPER improve protocol prespecification and reproducibility; they do not standardize longitudinal diagnostic summaries. Software ecosystems (cobalt, WeightIt, MatchIt, ipw, gfoRmula, lmtp, ltmle, adjustedCurves) supply balance, overlap, and weight diagnostics for specific designs, including some longitudinal use, but there is no field-wide agreed summary statistic for longitudinal balance or support-by-history, and no journal or regulator-mandated dashboard that makes omission of a panel a visible reporting failure. Method papers that propose or apply QBA, negative controls, or multi-panel diagnostics remain proposals or local practice, not an adopting-body convention. The core structural claim remains: conventions require adoption, and none has closed the reported gap. Queries included: assumption/diagnostic dashboard target trial; TARGET as diagnostic standard; longitudinal balance standardization cobalt WeightIt; ROBINS-I TTE diagnostics; STaRT-RWE HARPER assumption reporting 2024–2026; arXiv/medRxiv causal diagnostic checklist.

The claim is coherent and proportionate. It identifies a real gap in current reporting practice (no standard dashboard) and the rationale correctly identifies the structural reasons (lack of standardized measurements for longitudinal balance, need for an adopting body). This is a claim about current practice. I abstain on the status axis because verifying the current state of reporting practice requires evidence I cannot reach.

title: Calling an analysis a target trial emulation is treated as evidence about its assumption burden
statement: The assumptions an analysis needs form a ladder, and each step up adds one: from describing an association, to adjusting for measured confounders, to identifying a sustained-strategy effect, to transporting that effect to another population. A paper should identify the highest step its evidence plausibly reaches. In practice the label target trial emulation is doing that work instead: an analysis that adopts the framework is read as though it had climbed the ladder, when the framework secures the temporal alignment and nothing above it. The label has become a claim about credibility rather than a description of a design, and no convention exists for stating which step a given study actually reaches.
why_open: The framework's value is real, which is what makes the substitution durable: naming the target trial does prevent a class of self-inflicted biases, so the label is informative and is then over-read. There is no established vocabulary for the intermediate rungs, so an author wishing to be precise has to invent the terms. Reviewers and editors also use the label as a screening heuristic, which rewards using it and penalizes qualifying it.

prior_work.cite: Hubbard RA, Hernán MA. "Target trial emulation" for observational studies: potential and pitfalls. N Engl J Med 2024
prior_work.what_it_does: States what emulation does and does not secure, which is exactly the distinction the label erases in use.

prior_work.cite: Hansford HJ, et al. Reporting of observational studies explicitly aiming to emulate randomized trials: a systematic review. JAMA Netw Open 2023
prior_work.what_it_does: Finds that 43% of 200 studies claiming to emulate a trial did not describe all key emulation components, which measures how weakly the label constrains the practice.

proposed_direction: Publish an assumption-to-conclusion ladder with named rungs, and require every emulation to state which rung its evidence supports and what would be needed for the next one. Have journals ask for that statement rather than for the label, so that adopting the framework is reported as a design fact and credibility is argued separately. Audit a sample of published emulations against the ladder to establish the current distribution, since nobody presently knows how far the typical study reaches.
severity: The label now confers credibility it does not carry, across a fast-growing literature.

opinions.rationale: The underlying risk is real: naming a target trial does not establish causal identification. The proposed ladder is technically wrong, however, because the requirements are not nested one assumption at a time. Sustained strategies require history-specific consistency, sequential exchangeability, and sequential positivity, while transportability adds distinct population-exchangeability and support conditions. Target trial specification also contributes more than temporal alignment by defining the estimand and protocol components, although it guarantees none of those assumptions. The issue is critical only when the label substitutes for an explicit identification argument.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Target trial specification improves temporal alignment, protocol clarity, and estimand definition, but it does not establish consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity, valid measurement, correct estimation, or transportability. Studies should state these multidimensional requirements separately for the chosen estimand rather than claim a single assumption-ladder rung.

opinions.rationale: The claim is that the label target trial emulation is used as a credibility credential rather than as a design description of temporal alignment and protocol specification, and that no shared vocabulary states which step on an assumption-to-conclusion ladder a study reaches. Literature search under the inverted prior found restatements and measurements of this problem, not a solved convention. Hubbard and Hernán (N Engl J Med 2024) state what emulation does and does not secure, call sensitivity analysis for unobserved confounding essential, and explicitly deny that the framework is a panacea; that strengthens the conceptual distinction the problem describes and does not install a journal-level rung vocabulary or stop label-as-credibility use. Hansford et al. JAMA Netw Open 2023 quantifies weak adherence among studies that claim to emulate a trial (large fractions missing key components or dual protocol/emulation description), which shows the label does not bind practice. TARGET (2025) improves transparent reporting of the emulation claim and assumptions but does not replace the label with a required statement of the highest justified causal step, nor invent named intermediate rungs from association through measured confounding, sustained strategies, and transport. No 2024–2026 journal policy or reporting addendum was found that requires authors to declare an assumption ladder rung instead of (or in addition to) the TTE label, and no widely adopted named vocabulary for intermediate rungs was located. Commentaries that warn against over-reading TTE as causal certification reinforce that the misuse remains live. Proposal-stage ladders outside TTE (generic credibility ladders in other fields) do not solve the emulation-label problem as stated. Queries included: TTE label overused credibility; assumption ladder target trial; journal policy require emulation components 2024–2026; Hubbard Hernán potential pitfalls follow-on; TARGET vs causal claim strength.

The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. It describes a sociological dynamic where the TTE label substitutes for explicit assumption-burden statements. The rationale correctly identifies the structural reasons this persists (lack of vocabulary for intermediate rungs, institutional incentives). This is a claim about current practice. I abstain on the status axis because verifying reviewer and editor practices requires evidence I cannot reach.

title: Sequential emulation creates repeated participation and calendar-time confounding that its efficiency gain conceals
statement: Sequential emulation exploits repeated eligibility: a new trial is emulated at each decision point, and a person who is eligible at many points contributes to many trials. This uses the data better than a single baseline emulation and it introduces three complications together. The same person appears in many nested trials, so the observations are dependent in a way the pooled analysis must handle. Trials begun at different calendar times occur under different treatment availability, guidelines and background risk, so calendar time confounds the pooled contrast unless it is modeled. And a person's later eligibility is itself a consequence of earlier untreated survival, which links the trials causally rather than merely statistically. The efficiency gain is real and it is what makes these complications easy to overlook.
why_open: Pooling across trials requires an assumption that the effect is common across start times, which is exactly what calendar-time variation in practice makes doubtful, and testing it costs the efficiency the design was adopted for. The dependence is induced by the design rather than present in the data, so it has no natural clustering variable other than the person. Later eligibility conditional on earlier survival is a selection process, and whether it is innocuous depends on the outcome model being correct, which is the thing under test.

prior_work.cite: Caniglia EC, et al. Emulating target trials to avoid immortal time bias: an application to antibiotic initiation. Epidemiology 2023
prior_work.what_it_does: A worked sequential emulation showing how repeated decision points remove immortal time bias in a setting where treatment can begin at many times.

prior_work.cite: Su L, et al. TrialEmulation: an R package to emulate target trials for causal analysis of observational time-to-event data. arXiv 2024
prior_work.what_it_does: Implements the sequence expansion and censoring weights that the design requires, and documents the data expansion it produces.

proposed_direction: Model calendar time explicitly as an effect modifier rather than adjusting it away, and report the trial-specific estimates alongside the pooled one so that a pooled effect resting on incompatible start times is visible. Derive variance estimators that account for repeated participation by the same person across nested trials, and check their coverage against a bootstrap over persons. Establish whether the efficiency gain survives the correct variance treatment, since the case for the design rests on a comparison that has usually been made under the naive variance.
severity: Sequential emulation is becoming the default for treatments that can start at any time, and its dependence structure is routinely ignored.

source.locator: seed-linked.md line 298, the method-comparison row for sequential trial emulation, with the sequential-trial sources at line 330

opinions.rationale: The entry asks for variance estimators that account for repeated participation across nested trials and for a check of their coverage against a bootstrap over persons. That work has been done. A 2025 Statistical Methods in Medical Research paper compares confidence intervals for sequential trial emulation with survival outcomes across the sandwich variance estimator, nonparametric bootstrap, jackknife and a linearized estimating function bootstrap, and finds the last has better coverage in the small-sample, low-event-rate, low-treatment-prevalence regime that motivates the design. Sequential trials and marginal structural models were compared for survival outcomes in 2023. The dependence half of the entry is therefore substantially answered and should not be published as open. The calendar-time half, that pooling across start times assumes a common effect and that trial-specific estimates are not reported, is untouched by this work and survives.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Pooling across sequentially emulated trials assumes an effect common to start times that differ in treatment availability, guidelines and background risk, and trial-specific estimates are not conventionally reported alongside the pooled one.

resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Directly supplies and evaluates variance estimation for sequential trial emulation, including a computationally feasible bootstrap alternative, which is what the entry asks for as future work.

resolving_work.title: Causal inference in survival analysis using longitudinal observational data: sequential trials and marginal structural models
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Sets out the sequential-trials estimator alongside marginal structural models for survival outcomes, establishing the analysis the entry describes.

opinions.rationale: Repeated eligibility does create within-person dependence, but the pinned implementation already addresses the standard version of that problem: TrialEmulation clusters its sandwich covariance by the original person identifier. It also includes trial start period in the pooled outcome model by default and accepts user-specified trial-period formulas, including interactions for effect heterogeneity. Calendar time confounds a pooled person-trial contrast only when it predicts both treatment and outcome; treatment-effect variation across start times is a separate effect-modification issue. Likewise, only a pooled model constrained to one treatment coefficient assumes a common effect. Later eligibility changes the eligible survivor population, but this is part of the sequence of trial-specific protocols and does not make validity depend specifically on outcome-model correctness. The efficiency gain is also not guaranteed after accounting for correlation and variable weights. Remaining work concerns coverage when weights are estimated, finite-sample behavior, diagnostics for treatment-by-start-time heterogeneity, and clearly defined standardization across changing eligible populations. Those are legitimate methodological and reporting questions, but they do not support the asserted high-severity claim that basic variance and calendar-time methods are missing.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Sequential emulation can reuse eligible persons across trial starts, creating within-person correlation and potentially improving precision. Pooled analyses should cluster by person, model trial start flexibly, examine treatment-by-start-time heterogeneity, and consider a person-level bootstrap when uncertainty from estimated weights is material.

opinions.rationale: Inverted-prior search finds substantial 2024–2025 work on two of the three complications the entry bundles, so the problem is not open as a blank slate. On repeated participation and design-induced dependence, Limozin, Seaman and Su (arXiv 2407.08317; Stat Methods Med Res 2025) run a dedicated simulation comparing sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, linearised estimating-function bootstrap and jackknife CIs for marginal risk differences under sequential trial emulation (STE), explicitly because the same patient can enter many nested trials. They report that sandwich/bootstrap/jackknife can account for that correlation, that sandwich is conservative when weight uncertainty is ignored, and that LEF bootstrap has the best small/moderate-sample coverage. That is exactly the variance and person-level bootstrap coverage work the agenda’s “direction” asks for; TrialEmulation is the implementation vehicle they use. On calendar-time confounding of pooled contrasts, DeMonte, Shook-Sa and Hudgens (arXiv 2403.18115) formalize nested trial emulation when the effect is allowed to vary over calendar time and/or time since treatment, provide a trial-effect-homogeneity test, and estimate trial-specific as well as calendar-time-varying vaccine effectiveness. That is the “model calendar time as effect modifier and report trial-specific estimates alongside the pooled one” program, at least in the vaccine setting where calendar-time heterogeneity is most obvious. Keogh et al. (Stat Med 2023) already recommended formal tests of trial-by-covariate interactions and compared sequential-trial efficiency to MSM-IPTW. What remains open, and why this is only partial: (1) Limozin evaluates CI coverage and computation, not a definitive redesign verdict that the efficiency case for STE survives person-clustered variance in general applications; sandwich conservatism means naive SEs can still overstate precision relative to person-level resampling. (2) DeMonte’s calendar-time-varying MSMs are developed and simulated for nested vaccine trials; they do not close the problem for arbitrary sustained pharmacoepidemiologic strategies or for routine non-VE sequential emulations that still pool under a common-effect assumption. (3) The third arm (later eligibility as a consequence of earlier untreated survival, so that trials are causally linked and the selection process depends on the outcome model being correct) is not resolved by either paper; no 2024–2026 work found identifies that selection away or shows it is innocuous under weak conditions. Package activity (TrialEmulation, SEQTaRget on CRAN) implements expansion and weighting but does not by itself close the identification/inference gaps. Cited prior work (Caniglia 2023; Su arXiv 2402.12083) illustrates and software-izes the design rather than solving the three complications. Queries that returned no full solution: “sequential trial emulation selection later eligibility untreated survival”; “efficiency gain sequential nested trial person-cluster sandwich vs naive”; general-journal 2024–2026 searches for a single paper closing all three arms together. Net: variance and calendar-time arms are partially methodologically addressed with evaluated tools; the bundled “still open and easy to overlook” framing is still useful but overstates residual openness if it ignores Limozin 2025 and DeMonte 2024.

resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Provides NTE IPW estimators and MSMs that allow the effect to vary over calendar time and/or time since treatment, plus a formal test of trial effect homogeneity; estimates trial-specific and calendar-time-varying effects rather than only a pooled common effect. Partially closes the calendar-time confounding / pooled-contrast arm for nested trials (vaccine effectiveness setting).
resolving_work.quote: Typically, when nested trial emulation (NTE) is employed, effect estimates are pooled across trials to increase statistical efficiency. However, such pooled estimates may lack a clear interpretation when the treatment effect is heterogeneous across trials. ... COVID-19 VE may vary across trials due to calendar-time-specific factors like newly emerging viral strains and pandemic control policies. The TEH assumption can be assessed using a formal hypothesis test.

counter_evidence.quote: Despite the increasing popularity of TTE, there is a lack of research on different methods for constructing confidence intervals (CIs) of treatment effects in STE. ... In the more complex setting of STE, less attention appears to be paid to the development and evaluation of CI construction methods.

Often when NTE is used, treatment effect estimates are pooled across the emulated trials to increase statistical efficiency ... Such pooled estimates may lack a clear interpretation when the treatment effect is heterogeneous across trials.

opinions.rationale: The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. It identifies three genuine complications of sequential target trial emulation—design-induced dependence from repeated participation, calendar-time confounding across start times, and survival-conditioned later eligibility—and frames them as overlooked rather than impossible to address. The reasoning for openness is coherent: pooling requires a common-effect assumption that calendar-time variation challenges; the dependence has no natural clustering variable beyond the person; and the selection process depends on outcome-model correctness, which is the inferential target. None of these are asserted as structural impossibilities; they are framed as current-practice gaps, which is the correct register. The proposed directions (model calendar time as effect modifier, derive person-level variance estimators, compare efficiency under correct variance) are constructive and imply the problems are solvable, reinforcing that the claim is about practice rather than principle. The scope is appropriate: the claim does not say sequential emulation should be abandoned, only that its efficiency gain conceals complications that need methodological attention. The severity is proportionate to the cost of a wrong pooled estimate in a treatment-effect decision. I cannot verify whether specific software or recent papers already resolve all three complications together, so I do not downgrade from open, but the claim as stated does not depend on any software capability assertion.

dissent.rationale: Repeated eligibility does create within-person dependence, but the pinned implementation already addresses the standard version of that problem: TrialEmulation clusters its sandwich covariance by the original person identifier. It also includes trial start period in the pooled outcome model by default and accepts user-specified trial-period formulas, including interactions for effect heterogeneity. Calendar time confounds a pooled person-trial contrast only when it predicts both treatment and outcome; treatment-effect variation across start times is a separate effect-modification issue. Likewise, only a pooled model constrained to one treatment coefficient assumes a common effect. Later eligibility changes the eligible survivor population, but this is part of the sequence of trial-specific protocols and does not make validity depend specifically on outcome-model correctness. The efficiency gain is also not guaranteed after accounting for correlation and variable weights. Remaining work concerns coverage when weights are estimated, finite-sample behavior, diagnostics for treatment-by-start-time heterogeneity, and clearly defined standardization across changing eligible populations. Those are legitimate methodological and reporting questions, but they do not support the asserted high-severity claim that basic variance and calendar-time methods are missing.

evidence.title: Assessing COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness in observational studies via nested trial emulation
evidence.what_it_resolves: Provides NTE IPW estimators and MSMs that allow the effect to vary over calendar time and/or time since treatment, plus a formal test of trial effect homogeneity; estimates trial-specific and calendar-time-varying effects rather than only a pooled common effect. evidence.quote: Typically, when nested trial emulation (NTE) is employed, effect estimates are pooled across trials to increase statistical efficiency. However, such pooled estimates may lack a clear interpretation when the treatment effect is heterogeneous across trials. ... COVID-19 VE may vary across trials due to calendar-time-specific factors like newly emerging viral strains and pandemic control policies. The TEH assumption can be assessed using a formal hypothesis test.

dissent.rationale: Inverted-prior search finds substantial 2024–2025 work on two of the three complications the entry bundles, so the problem is not open as a blank slate. On repeated participation and design-induced dependence, Limozin, Seaman and Su (arXiv 2407.08317; Stat Methods Med Res 2025) run a dedicated simulation comparing sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, linearised estimating-function bootstrap and jackknife CIs for marginal risk differences under sequential trial emulation (STE), explicitly because the same patient can enter many nested trials. They report that sandwich/bootstrap/jackknife can account for that correlation, that sandwich is conservative when weight uncertainty is ignored, and that LEF bootstrap has the best small/moderate-sample coverage. That is exactly the variance and person-level bootstrap coverage work the agenda’s “direction” asks for; TrialEmulation is the implementation vehicle they use. On calendar-time confounding of pooled contrasts, DeMonte, Shook-Sa and Hudgens (arXiv 2403.18115) formalize nested trial emulation when the effect is allowed to vary over calendar time and/or time since treatment, provide a trial-effect-homogeneity test, and estimate trial-specific as well as calendar-time-varying vaccine effectiveness. That is the “model calendar time as effect modifier and report trial-specific estimates alongside the pooled one” program, at least in the vaccine setting where calendar-time heterogeneity is most obvious. Keogh et al. (Stat Med 2023) already recommended formal tests of trial-by-covariate interactions and compared sequential-trial efficiency to MSM-IPTW. What remains open, and why this is only partial: (1) Limozin evaluates CI coverage and computation, not a definitive redesign verdict that the efficiency case for STE survives person-clustered variance in general applications; sandwich conservatism means naive SEs can still overstate precision relative to person-level resampling. (2) DeMonte’s calendar-time-varying MSMs are developed and simulated for nested vaccine trials; they do not close the problem for arbitrary sustained pharmacoepidemiologic strategies or for routine non-VE sequential emulations that still pool under a common-effect assumption. (3) The third arm (later eligibility as a consequence of earlier untreated survival, so that trials are causally linked and the selection process depends on the outcome model being correct) is not resolved by either paper; no 2024–2026 work found identifies that selection away or shows it is innocuous under weak conditions. Package activity (TrialEmulation, SEQTaRget on CRAN) implements expansion and weighting but does not by itself close the identification/inference gaps. Cited prior work (Caniglia 2023; Su arXiv 2402.12083) illustrates and software-izes the design rather than solving the three complications. Queries that returned no full solution: “sequential trial emulation selection later eligibility untreated survival”; “efficiency gain sequential nested trial person-cluster sandwich vs naive”; general-journal 2024–2026 searches for a single paper closing all three arms together. Net: variance and calendar-time arms are partially methodologically addressed with evaluated tools; the bundled “still open and easy to overlook” framing is still useful but overstates residual openness if it ignores Limozin 2025 and DeMonte 2024.

title: Variance estimation after cloning and sequence expansion has no scalable, correct default
statement: Sequential emulation and cloning expand a dataset by orders of magnitude: each person contributes a row per eligible decision point, and cloning multiplies that by the number of strategies with which the person is initially compatible. Two dependence structures result. Repeated eligibility means a person appears in many trials, and cloning means several rows are copies of the same person's history. Naive standard errors ignore both. The bootstrap is correct in principle and often prohibitive at this scale, particularly with flexible nuisance models that must be refitted per replicate. The `TrialEmulation` package supports sequence expansion, censoring weights, outcome models and chunked processing, and general scalable variance estimation for this design remains unsettled.
why_open: The dependence is nested rather than simply clustered: clones within a person within a site, with the clone-level dependence induced by the analysis rather than present in the data. Influence-function variance estimators need the influence function of the full estimator including the weight-estimation step, which is not available in closed form once the nuisance models are learned. Every workaround trades in the same currency, since subsampling to make the bootstrap affordable reintroduces the finite-sample instability the bootstrap was there to characterize.

prior_work.cite: Su L, et al. TrialEmulation: an R package to emulate target trials for causal analysis of observational time-to-event data. arXiv 2024
prior_work.what_it_does: Implements sequence expansion, censoring-weight calculation and outcome models for intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses, with chunked processing for the data expansion.

prior_work.cite: TrialEmulation getting-started vignette
prior_work.what_it_does: Documents the all-in-one initiators() workflow and the modular functions, which is the reference implementation practitioners actually use.

proposed_direction: Derive influence-function and multiplier-bootstrap variance estimators clustered by original individual and by site, so that the clone-level dependence created by the analysis is handled where it is created. Support the scale with streaming risk-set construction, columnar back ends such as DuckDB or Arrow, sparse history representations, and case-control sampling with proven error control rather than heuristic subsampling. Report coverage under the actual dependence structure rather than under independence, because the failure this produces is anticonservative and therefore invisible in a point estimate.
severity: Anticonservative intervals from a computationally convenient variance estimator are indistinguishable from precision.

opinions.rationale: The variance problem for the sequence-expansion half of this entry has been addressed: a 2025 paper compares sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, jackknife and linearized estimating function bootstrap confidence intervals for sequential trial emulation with survival outcomes and finds a computationally feasible option with better coverage in the motivating regime. The entry should not present that as open. The cloning half is not covered by that work, and a search for variance estimation under cloning specifically returned nothing, so the dependence induced by copies of the same person remains unaddressed. The computational directions the entry proposes, streaming risk sets and columnar back ends, appear nowhere in the corpus.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Variance estimation for sequence expansion has been studied and a feasible recommendation exists; variance under cloning, where several rows are copies of one person's history, has not been addressed, and no scalable implementation strategy is published.
