resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Supplies and evaluates variance estimation for sequence expansion, including a bootstrap alternative fast enough to run.

opinions.rationale: The full-estimator variance problem remains real, but the stated rationale overreaches. Rows created by repeated eligibility or cloning remain within the original individual, so clustering on that individual handles arbitrary dependence among those rows; clone dependence is not a separate sampling level. The pinned TrialEmulation source automatically computes a person-clustered sandwich covariance for its fitted MSM, providing a scalable analytic default for the outcome-model estimating equation. It does not propagate uncertainty from estimated switching or censoring weights, flexible nuisance learning, or site-level sampling. If sites are the independent units, inference should generally cluster or resample sites rather than treat clones-within-person-within-site as an exotic multiway structure. Likewise, a bootstrap is valid only when it resamples the appropriate independent unit and refits the full pipeline. A learner-specific closed-form influence function is also not universally necessary for orthogonal, cross-fitted estimators under suitable rate conditions.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Person-clustered sandwich inference provides a scalable way to handle dependence created by repeated eligibility and cloning when weights are fixed or the relevant estimating-equation conditions hold. A general default that also propagates estimated-weight and flexible-nuisance uncertainty, and that accommodates site-level sampling where applicable, remains unsettled.

opinions.rationale:
Inverted prior: assume scalable correct variance already exists. Highest-yield hit is Limozin, Seaman, and Su (SMMR 2025; arXiv 2407.08317), co-authored with the TrialEmulation lead: they compare sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, jackknife, and a new LEF bootstrap for sequential trial emulation (STE) marginal risk differences under IPW. LEF is faster than full bootstrap and covers better under the sparse regimes that motivate STE; sandwich is fastest and covers well only with large n and medium/high event rates. They state explicitly that sandwich is the only CI method in TrialEmulation and that it ignores weight-estimation uncertainty. That is real progress on the sequential-eligibility half of the claim.

It does not close the problem as stated. Coverage guidance is setting-specific, not a single default. LEF is research code (GitHub simulation repo), not a TrialEmulation default. The design is parametric MSM/IPW STE, not nested clone-within-person-within-site dependence from multi-strategy cloning, and not influence functions for flexible nuisance models. Clone-censor-weight primers (Gaber et al. 2024; Webster-Clark et al. PDS 2025; survivalCCW) still recommend bootstrap or robust SE and ship bootstrap vignettes; they do not deliver streaming IF or Arrow/DuckDB risk-set variance. Queries run: sequential trial variance sandwich bootstrap jackknife; clone-censor-weight variance; TrialEmulation robust SE; arXiv 2407.08317; survivalCCW; Enders 2018 sandwich (still not off-the-shelf). No 2025–2026 package release supplies a general scalable correct default for both cloning and sequence expansion under flexible nuisances. Partial solve of STE inference guidance; core gap remains.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: For parametric MSM sequential trial emulation with IPW, evaluated options now exist (person-clustered sandwich, LEF bootstrap, jackknife, nonparametric bootstrap) with simulation guidance on coverage versus cost, but there is still no scalable default that correctly handles cloning-induced clone-level dependence, site clustering, and weight estimation under flexible nuisance models at sequence-expansion scale.

opinions.rationale: The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. It does not assert impossibility; it says the problem 'remains unsettled,' which is a claim about the state of methodology and practice. The reason given for openness—nested dependence (clones within persons within sites) and the lack of closed-form influence functions once nuisance models are learned—is a genuine methodological gap that structurally supports the claim being open. The acknowledgment that the bootstrap is 'correct in principle' but 'often prohibitive' is a fair characterization of a practical tradeoff rather than an overstatement. I cannot verify what the TrialEmulation package does or does not implement, but the core methodological claim about the absence of a scalable, correct default variance estimator for this design is coherent and the stated reasons entail openness. The claim about software capabilities is not the load-bearing part of the argument; the load-bearing part is the identifiability/derivability of the influence function under learned nuisance models, which is a methodological claim I can assess for coherence.

title: Generative models are evaluated on distributional fidelity and used for causal work
statement: Generative patient models would support privacy-preserving code development, power planning and method stress testing, and synthetic patient data have shown value as a benchmark environment. The evaluation practice does not match the use. A model optimized for marginal or temporal fidelity can reproduce every observed association while generating wrong counterfactuals, wrong overlap and wrong time ordering, because none of those quantities appears in the loss. Privacy mechanisms compound this by suppressing rare patterns, and rare patterns are often exactly the causally important ones. Synthetic data are not evidence about treatment effects unless the generating model is causally valid, and current benchmarks do not test whether it is.
why_open: Causal fidelity is not identifiable from the observed data the generator was trained on: two structural models that agree on every observational distribution can disagree on every interventional one. Evaluating it therefore requires a gold-standard structural model rather than a real dataset, which changes the object being validated. Privacy and causal fidelity are also in direct tension, since the mechanisms that protect rare individuals remove the rare strata that carry the overlap.

prior_work.cite: Shi, et al. Generating high-fidelity privacy-conscious synthetic patient data for causal effect estimation with multiple treatments. Front Artif Intell 2022
prior_work.what_it_does: Builds synthetic patient generation aimed specifically at causal effect estimation with multiple treatments, which is where the fidelity question becomes sharp.

proposed_direction: Create causally annotated synthetic trials in which both observed and counterfactual outcomes are generated from a known structural model, so that interventional distributions have a ground truth to be scored against. Evaluate generative models on intervention response error, average and conditional effect fidelity, positivity preservation and disclosure risk, not only on distributional similarity. State as a standing rule that synthetic-effect estimates are not clinical evidence, and confine synthetic data to code development, power planning and method benchmarking.
severity: The misuse is easy, the evaluation gap is invisible, and the output looks like data.

opinions.rationale: The central warning is correct: observational distributional fidelity alone does not establish counterfactual fidelity. The impossibility argument is nevertheless too broad. Observationally equivalent causal models can disagree on some interventions, not necessarily every intervention. Interventional distributions can also be identified under explicit causal assumptions or evaluated using randomized or other interventional data, so a known structural simulator is not the only possible benchmark. Positivity and treatment overlap are properties of the observed longitudinal law; a generator that exactly preserves the full joint law preserves them, although marginal-fidelity metrics can miss serious conditional-support errors. Temporal ordering is likewise observable and testable. Privacy protection creates a utility tradeoff for rare strata but does not invariably remove them or create a direct mathematical conflict with causal fidelity.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Marginal or superficial temporal fidelity does not validate a generator's counterfactual behavior. Without identifying causal assumptions or interventional ground truth, observationally indistinguishable generators can disagree on some interventions. Causal benchmarks should therefore use an explicit structural data-generating model or external interventional evidence and should assess conditional support, longitudinal ordering, effect fidelity, and privacy loss separately.

Amad et al. Partial solve of evaluation methodology; the practice mismatch remains open.

opinions.rationale: The claim is structurally sound and proportionate. The core identifiability argument—that two structural models agreeing on every observational distribution can disagree on every interventional one—is a well-established result in causal inference and correctly grounds the claim that causal fidelity cannot be assessed from observational data alone. The claim does not assert that causally valid generators are impossible to build; it asserts that current benchmarks do not test for causal validity, which is a claim about practice, not about impossibility. The tension between privacy mechanisms and causal fidelity (suppression of rare patterns that carry overlap) is a genuine practical tradeoff, correctly framed as tension rather than impossibility. The standing rule proposed—that synthetic-effect estimates are not clinical evidence—is proportionate to the severity of the error (clinical decisions based on non-causally-valid synthetic data). The scope is right: the claim is about evaluation practice, not about the existence of generative models per se.

title: Code, phenotype logic, weight diagnostics and rejected protocol versions are not available for emulations
statement: The TARGET statement asks for the target protocol, its data mapping, the estimands, the assumptions, the estimates and the sensitivity analyses, and it is a transparency instrument rather than a risk-of-bias certification. What remains unavailable in practice is the material that would let someone re-run the study: the analysis code, the complete phenotype logic including the code lists and their versions, the weight diagnostics, and the protocol versions that were tried and rejected. An emulation is a long pipeline in which most of the decisions are expressed in code rather than in prose, so a paper that reports the protocol faithfully can still be irreproducible in every operative detail.
why_open: Phenotype logic is often held under license or embedded in institutional tooling, so publishing it is a legal and technical problem rather than a willingness problem. Analysis code for a longitudinal emulation depends on a data model the reader cannot obtain, which makes released code unrunnable and therefore feel pointless to release. Rejected protocol versions are not artifacts anyone currently keeps, so there is nothing to publish even when there is a will to.

prior_work.cite: Hansford HJ, Cashin AG, Jones MD, et al. Transparent reporting of observational studies emulating a target trial: the TARGET statement. JAMA 2025
prior_work.what_it_does: Establishes the reporting standard for emulations, whose purpose is transparency rather than risk-of-bias certification.

proposed_direction: Publish machine-readable protocols, complete phenotype logic with code-set versions, simulated test data that exercises the pipeline, a containerized environment and an executable reproduction report that runs end to end on the simulated data. Pair the TARGET checklist with RECORD and STROBE and with a causal risk-of-bias assessment, so that reporting, provenance and appraisal are separately satisfied. Treat the simulated test dataset as the deliverable that makes released code meaningful when the real data cannot leave the institution.
severity: Emulations are being used in regulatory and guideline decisions while remaining unreproducible in their operative detail.

opinions.rationale: The reproducibility objective is technically sound, but the report turns a variable practice deficit into a universal claim. Code tied to an inaccessible data model is still useful when accompanied by a schema, adapters, containers, or synthetic fixtures. Version control and protocol registries can retain amendments, so it is false that rejected versions are artifacts nobody keeps. Synthetic test data can establish executability and exercise phenotype and weighting logic, but cannot reproduce or validate the real-data estimate. Final analysis code, versioned phenotype definitions, and weight diagnostics are decision-critical; publication of every discarded draft is a lower-priority provenance demand and is better framed as a prospective amendment and decision log. The pinned TrialEmulation source supports the narrower claim that reusable sequence-expansion and weighting machinery exists, but it cannot supply study-specific phenotype logic or release artifacts.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: An emulation is not externally auditable when its final analysis code, complete versioned phenotype logic, and weight diagnostics are unavailable. When real data cannot be shared, code plus a documented schema, container, and synthetic fixtures can establish executability but cannot reproduce the published estimate; material protocol amendments should be retained in a versioned decision log.

opinions.rationale:
Inverted prior: assume executable code, versioned phenotypes, weight diagnostics, and rejected protocols are already standard deliverables. TARGET (Cashin/Hansford et al., JAMA/BMJ 2025) is correctly scoped as a reporting checklist for protocol, mapping, estimands, assumptions, estimates, and sensitivity analyses; it is not a risk-of-bias instrument and does not require analysis code, code-list versions, weight diagnostics dumps, or failed protocol versions. That part of the claim stands.

Partial prior art exists in infrastructure, not in universal publication norms. OHDSI Phenotype Library is a public, version-controlled phenotype repository with release versioning and DOIs for cohort definitions (partial answer to phenotype logic and code-set versions, limited to OMOP/OHDSI contributors). Strategus/HADES encode analyses as shareable JSON-plus-R workflows on OMOP. THESEUS (Kim et al., medRxiv 2026.03.13.26348306) automates mapping free-text TTE descriptions to Strategus JSON and executable R, improving shareable machine-readable specs for OHDSI-style studies; it does not compel release of rejected protocols or non-OMOP phenotype licenses. Scattered tutorials (e.g. Hoffman steroids-trial-emulation with simulated data) and TrialEmulation show that reference code can be released, which does not make re-runnable artifacts common for applied emulations on licensed claims/EHR. Queries run: TARGET reproducibility code phenotype; OHDSI Phenotype Library; THESEUS Strategus TTE; STaRT-RWE HARPER code sharing; RECORD-PE STROBE rejected protocol versions. No 2025–2026 guidance requires publishing rejected protocol versions or institution-exportable simulated test datasets as the standard companion to TARGET. Legal and data-model barriers named in the problem remain. title: No procedure defines clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions
statement: A per-protocol effect requires censoring at deviation and weighting for the informative censoring that censoring creates. Beneath that mechanics sits a question the mechanics assume away: what counts as the same treatment. Real treatments differ by dose, route, provider, formulation, combination and adherence pattern, and two regimens sharing a label may not satisfy consistency. Clone-censor-weight handles the case where baseline assignment is genuinely ambiguous, at the cost of data expansion, artificial censoring and sensitivity to the censoring model, but it takes the strategy definition as given. There is no guidance for constructing defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions, and none for overlapping combination therapies where a patient is simultaneously compatible with more than one labeled strategy.
why_open: Consistency is an assumption about the world rather than about the data, so no amount of data adjudicates whether two versions are the same treatment. The clinical judgment that would adjudicate it is specific to the drug, the indication and the era, which makes a general criterion the wrong shape for the problem. Making the versions explicit also multiplies the strategies, and each additional strategy costs positivity, so the honest specification is often the one the data cannot support.

prior_work.cite: Gaber CE, Ghazarian AA, Strassle PD, et al. De-mystifying the clone-censor-weight method for causal research using observational data. Cancer Med 2024
prior_work.what_it_does: A didactic account of cloning, artificial censoring and censoring weights, including the computational cost and the sensitivity to the censoring model.

prior_work.cite: Cain LE, Robins JM, Lanoy E, Logan R, Costagliola D, Hernán MA. Using observational data to emulate a randomized trial of dynamic treatment-switching strategies. Int J Epidemiol 2016;45(6):2038-2049
prior_work.what_it_does: Defines dynamic switching strategies precisely enough to emulate, which is the closest existing template for specifying what a strategy includes.

prior_work.cite: lmtp: Non-Parametric Causal Effects of Feasible Interventions Based on Modified Treatment Policies. CRAN
prior_work.what_it_does: Supports continuous and multivariate treatments, which is the representation a dose-and-adherence strategy needs.

proposed_direction: Use hierarchical treatment ontologies and latent treatment-version models so that the equivalence class is an explicit, versioned object rather than an implicit one, and estimate the joint effect of initiation, dose and adherence through longitudinal modified treatment policies rather than through a single binary strategy. Use causal discovery only to generate hypotheses about which versions are consequential; final strategy definitions must stay clinically specified, because a version set chosen to maximize the apparent effect is a result rather than a design. Quantify, by simulation, how much bias a wrong equivalence class induces relative to the positivity cost of the correct one, since that trade is the actual decision.
severity: Consistency failures are invisible in the output: the estimate is precise and the estimand is not the one named.

source.locator: seed-linked.md line 70, row 'Adherence, switching, discontinuation and multiple treatment versions'

opinions.rationale: The treatment-versions problem has a longer literature than the entry credits. Confounding adjustment in the presence of multiple versions of treatment was worked out for an organ-transplant application in 2019, and marginal structural models for partial exposure regimes date to 2008. A 2026 iScience paper shows that changing the exposure definition unmasks confounding in an applied emulation, which is empirical evidence for the entry's premise and also evidence that the field is examining it. What remains genuinely absent is guidance for constructing defensible equivalence classes and for overlapping combination therapies, which is the constructive half of the entry rather than the diagnostic half.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Estimation under multiple versions of treatment has been formalized, and there is no guidance for deciding which versions form a defensible equivalence class, nor for strategies with which a patient is simultaneously compatible.

resolving_work.title: The meaning of confounding adjustment in the presence of multiple versions of treatment: an application to organ transplantation
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Works out what adjustment means when a labeled treatment covers several versions, which the entry treats as unaddressed.

resolving_work.title: Marginal structural models for partial exposure regimes
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Provides estimation for regimes that specify treatment only partially, which is the representation an underspecified strategy needs.

resolving_work.title: Exposure definition sensitivity unmasks hidden confounding in crystalloid target trial emulation
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Shows empirically that the exposure definition changes the answer in an emulation, which is the consequence the entry predicts.

opinions.rationale: Treatment-version ambiguity is real: collapsing causally different doses, formulations, routes, combinations, or adherence patterns can make the named intervention ill-defined. However, the report overstates both the required mechanics and the remaining gap. Estimating a per-protocol effect does not require artificial censoring plus inverse-probability weighting; the longitudinal g-formula and targeted or sequential-regression estimators can estimate sustained-strategy effects under their respective identification and modeling conditions. Clone-censor-weight already provides the bookkeeping for individuals compatible with multiple prespecified strategies, although it cannot choose those strategies or determine which versions are equivalent. Observed data cannot prove treatment-version irrelevance, but version-specific data can reveal heterogeneity and inform clinical judgment. Finer definitions may worsen practical support and precision, but every additional strategy does not mechanically violate positivity. Pinned lmtp 1.5.4 is correctly described: its NAMESPACE exports lmtp_tmle and lmtp_sdr, while its source accepts list-valued treatment nodes and applies analyst-specified multivariate shifts. It therefore supports estimation after a joint policy has been defined, not construction of clinical equivalence classes. Moreover, a longitudinal modified treatment policy generally targets a natural-value-dependent policy estimand, not automatically the per-protocol effect of a fixed sustained strategy. The issue is decision-critical when collapsed versions have materially different effects; a universal treatment ontology or latent-version model is a roadmap item rather than a prerequisite for every well-specified emulation.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Analysts must clinically specify sustained strategies and relevant treatment versions before estimating a per-protocol effect. Artificial censoring and inverse-probability weighting are one valid estimation approach, not a universal requirement. Clone-censor-weight handles individuals compatible with multiple predefined strategies but does not determine whether treatment versions should be pooled. Observed data alone cannot establish treatment-version irrelevance, although they can expose heterogeneity, and finer definitions may create practical support problems. Longitudinal multivariate modified-treatment-policy estimators can estimate an analyst-specified joint policy but do not supply the clinical equivalence classes or necessarily target the same per-protocol estimand.

resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Provides the cloning, artificial-censoring, and weighting procedure for individuals whose observed histories are simultaneously compatible with multiple predefined strategies. It does not determine which treatment versions should constitute a strategy.

resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Pinned source exports longitudinal TMLE and sequentially doubly robust estimators and implements analyst-specified multivariate treatment shifts. This resolves the joint-policy estimation component after treatment variables and the intervention have been defined, but not equivalence-class construction.

opinions.rationale: Inverted-prior search does not find a procedure that constructs clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions for consistency in sustained-strategy target-trial emulation. The report’s own cited works do not close the gap: Gaber et al. (2024, 10.1002/cam4.70461) is a didactic CCW primer that takes the strategy as given; Cain et al. (2016, 10.1093/ije/dyv295) is the closest specification template for dynamic switching but does not adjudicate dose, route, formulation, provider, or combination-version equivalence; lmtp supplies estimation for continuous and multivariate modified treatment policies once an intervention is defined, not a clinical rule for which versions may be labeled the same treatment. Classic prior art formalizes the identification problem without solving clinical construction: VanderWeele and Hernán (2013, J Causal Inference; multiple versions) and Hernán and VanderWeele (2011, compound treatments) show when version-mixed averages versus version-specific effects are identifiable, which strengthens rather than resolves the claim that consistency is a world assumption adjudicated by clinical judgment specific to drug, indication, and era. 2024–2026 work remains proposal-level or off-scope. Yoshikawa and Kawano (arXiv:2601.00287, 2026) propose mixture-of-experts estimation of latent versions under point treatment; the number of versions is pre-specified, versions are data-driven latent classes rather than clinically specified equivalence classes, and the paper itself notes that version-specific methodology was previously underdeveloped. That is a partial advance along the report’s proposed latent-version direction, not a solved clinical procedure, and it does not cover sustained or dynamic strategies or overlapping multi-drug regimens. Ostropolets et al. (2024) ATC–RxNorm hierarchies improve drug coding and retrieval; they are not causal equivalence classes for consistency. Fu et al. (BMJ 2026) and related CCW guidance clarify cloning when baseline data are compatible with more than one labeled strategy; that is the mechanics the report already credits, still leaving strategy definition as input. Practical TTE guides (e.g. Fridén 2026) restate “define interventions so relevant multiple versions do not exist” without a constructive algorithm. Package release notes and GitHub activity for TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, ltmle, WeightIt, MatchIt, and related tools implement estimation given a user-defined regimen; none encode an equivalence-class constructor. 2025–2026 FDA RWE / externally controlled trial materials, EMA/HMA registry guidance, HARPER/STaRT-RWE, ENCePP, and TARGET-style reporting require explicit treatment-strategy specification but do not supply a general method for building clinically defensible version sets or for adjudicating simultaneous multi-strategy compatibility beyond cloning. Because consistency is structurally untestable from data alone, sensitivity analyses and latent-mixture recoveries quantify consequences or statistical heterogeneity; they do not identify clinical sameness. Queries that returned nothing closing the gap included combinations of: treatment version equivalence class + target trial; clinically defensible versions of treatment + consistency; hierarchical ontology + causal strategy definition + sustained treatment; overlapping combination therapy + clone-censor equivalence; and journal-restricted 2024–2026 searches in AJE, Epidemiology, IJE, Stat Med, Biometrics, BMJ, JAMA, plus arXiv stat.ME and medRxiv. Residual risk is a narrowly scoped clinical protocol for one drug class that was not indexed under causal-inference terms; that would at most partially narrow the problem for that class, not the general gap as stated.

The claim is internally consistent and identifies a genuine structural tension: consistency is an assumption about the world, not the data, so clinical adjudication of treatment-version equivalence is inherently context-specific (drug, indication, era). The report's own reasoning—that 'a general criterion [is] the wrong shape for the problem'—supports a structural impossibility for a universal procedure, which is a stronger and more defensible claim than the empirical assertion that 'no guidance exists.' The latter is a negative existential about the current literature that I cannot verify without search. Additionally, the report itself cites Cain et al. 2016 as 'the closest existing template for specifying what a strategy includes,' which suggests related guidance exists even if it does not directly address equivalence-class construction. The claim is pitched at a level that conflates a structural limitation (no general procedure can work) with an empirical gap (no guidance has been written), and the proposed direction (ontologies, latent models, modified treatment policies) implies that partial frameworks are possible, undercutting the implication that the problem is permanently intractable. The severity is proportionate: a wrong equivalence class induces bias, and the positivity trade-off is a real decision cost. I abstain on status because confirming the absence of all guidance requires literature search I cannot perform.

dissent.rationale: Treatment-version ambiguity is real: collapsing causally different doses, formulations, routes, combinations, or adherence patterns can make the named intervention ill-defined. However, the report overstates both the required mechanics and the remaining gap. Estimating a per-protocol effect does not require artificial censoring plus inverse-probability weighting; the longitudinal g-formula and targeted or sequential-regression estimators can estimate sustained-strategy effects under their respective identification and modeling conditions. Clone-censor-weight already provides the bookkeeping for individuals compatible with multiple prespecified strategies, although it cannot choose those strategies or determine which versions are equivalent. Observed data cannot prove treatment-version irrelevance, but version-specific data can reveal heterogeneity and inform clinical judgment. Finer definitions may worsen practical support and precision, but every additional strategy does not mechanically violate positivity. Pinned lmtp 1.5.4 is correctly described: its NAMESPACE exports lmtp_tmle and lmtp_sdr, while its source accepts list-valued treatment nodes and applies analyst-specified multivariate shifts. It therefore supports estimation after a joint policy has been defined, not construction of clinical equivalence classes. Moreover, a longitudinal modified treatment policy generally targets a natural-value-dependent policy estimand, not automatically the per-protocol effect of a fixed sustained strategy. The issue is decision-critical when collapsed versions have materially different effects; a universal treatment ontology or latent-version model is a roadmap item rather than a prerequisite for every well-specified emulation.

title: Negative controls, proxies and validation data are not integrated into a standard emulation workflow
statement: Specifying a target trial prevents the temporal biases an analyst inflicts on themselves; it does not create randomization. Active-comparator new-user designs, high-dimensional propensity scores and richer clinical measurements all reduce residual confounding without guaranteeing exchangeability. The tools that address what remains, negative control outcomes and exposures, instrumental variables, proximal causal learning and external validation samples, exist separately and are not part of any standard emulation workflow: there is no agreed order in which to apply them, no convention for reporting what each one bought, and no accepted way to combine their answers when they disagree. Covariate balance continues to be reported as though it bore on unmeasured confounding, which it does not.
why_open: Each of these tools identifies under assumptions that are themselves untestable and that differ from one another, so combining them is not a matter of adding evidence but of reconciling incompatible identification stories. A negative control shares only some of the confounding mechanisms of the primary outcome, and how much is not knowable from the data. Proximal methods need proxies satisfying completeness-type conditions that cannot be checked, and weak proxies produce unstable estimates that look like precision loss rather than assumption failure. Validation subsamples are rarely random, which imports a second selection problem into the correction for the first.

prior_work.cite: Hernán MA, Robins JM. Using big data to emulate a target trial when a randomized trial is not available. Am J Epidemiol 2016;183(8):758-764
prior_work.what_it_does: The foundational framework: it specifies the seven protocol components and their observational mapping, and locates confounding outside what the framework itself resolves.

proposed_direction: Develop a proximal emulation in which treatment-inducing and outcome-inducing proxies are declared in the protocol alongside the negative controls, and estimate the primary effect under the proximal identification conditions as well as the conventional ones. Report the conventional estimate next to E-values, bias functions, Rosenbaum-style sensitivity models, tipping-point analyses and priors on unmeasured confounding, all keyed to the same estimand so the reader sees one quantity under several assumption sets. Establish, by simulation, how far negative-control calibration transfers when the control shares only part of the confounding structure, because that is the assumption the method makes and never states.
severity: This is the assumption on which every emulation ultimately rests and the one the framework does nothing to secure.

opinions.rationale: Searching for an integrated workflow combining negative controls, proxies, instrumental variables and validation data within an emulation returned applied studies that use one of these tools, not a workflow that orders or combines them. opinions.rationale: The integration and reporting problem is legitimate, but several technical absolutes are wrong. Merely specifying a target trial does not prevent temporal bias; correct time-zero alignment and implementation can prevent particular design-induced biases. Active-comparator new-user designs, high-dimensional propensity scores, and richer measurements are not guaranteed to reduce confounding and can introduce bias through poor comparator or variable selection. Negative controls often diagnose or falsify rather than identify a corrected effect. Instrument relevance and some proxy-strength or rank features are assessable even though exclusion, proxy validity, and completeness relative to latent confounding are not fully testable. IV, proximal, and conventional analyses can also target different estimands, so E-values, Rosenbaum analyses, bias functions, and causal estimates are not automatically commensurate answers about one quantity. Balance on ordinary measured covariates cannot establish balance on unmeasured confounders, although validated proxies can provide indirect information. Residual confounding is decision-critical, but the absence of one universal integration workflow is primarily a standardization and triangulation problem; the asserted very-high severity and claim that the framework does nothing to secure exchangeability are inflated. No R or Python package capability is asserted here.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: A correctly implemented target-trial emulation can prevent specific design-induced temporal biases but does not create exchangeability. Negative controls, instrumental variables, proximal methods, and validation data address residual confounding under distinct, partly untestable assumptions and sometimes different estimands; they cannot be mechanically ordered or combined without an explicit estimand-aligned joint model. Balance on ordinary measured covariates alone does not establish balance on unmeasured confounders.

opinions.rationale: Inverted-prior search treated the gap as already closed and looked for a field-standard emulation pipeline that declares negative controls, treatment/outcome proxies, proximal identification, instruments, and validation samples in the protocol, reports what each tool bought on a shared estimand, and reconciles disagreements. That standard was not found. The cited works (Hubbard–Hernán 2024; Hernán–Robins 2016) correctly locate residual confounding outside protocol design; they do not integrate residual-confounding tools into a workflow. Recent literature and software add components and occasional applications, not a consensus order or combination rule. Guo et al. (2025) run a target trial emulation under proximal causal inference with declared NCE/NCO proxies and sensitivity swaps of those controls: that is a serious applied fusion of TTE and PCI, not a field standard or a protocol template for combining PCI with E-values, bias functions, Rosenbaum models, tipping points, and external validation on one estimand. BenchExCal (Wang et al. 2025) proposes a structured benchmark–expand–calibration process that uses negative-control calibration in an emulation pipeline; the paper is a design and planned evaluation, not an established convention. Practical TTE checklists and operational EHR frameworks (e.g., Tran 2026; Nature Digital Medicine operational TTE 2026) recommend negative-control diagnostics, which softens the claim that residual tools are invisible in guidance, but still treat them as optional diagnostics rather than protocol-declared primary analyses. TARGET (JAMA 2025) is a reporting checklist for emulations; it does not prescribe proximal protocols or multi-tool reconciliation. CRAN task-view and package checks (TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, ltmle, WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt, PCL) show no merged standard that wires NCO panels, proximal estimation, validation-sample correction, and conventional estimands into one emulation API. Distributional NCO diagnosis/calibration work on medRxiv (2026) is a proposal. Sensitivity and proximal methods still rest on untestable, non-identical identification stories; papers that propose or apply methods do not solve combination under disagreement. Covariate balance remains widely reported without claiming identification of unmeasured confounding in the sources retrieved. Queries run: TTE+proximal; NCO calibration/BenchExCal/TARGET; PCI software (PCL, regression-based PCI); package/CRAN activity for TrialEmulation/gfoRmula/lmtp; guidance (TARGET, ENCePP, ICH). Net: the problem as stated (no agreed integrated residual-confounding workflow for emulations) remains open; the caveat is that TTE+PCI applications and NCO-centric calibration proposals now exist and should be cited as prior art, not as closure.

counter_evidence.quote: We integrated the target trial emulation (TTE) framework with the proximal causal inference (PCI) approach, a novel method proposed to correct unmeasured confounding through the use of negative controls as measured proxies of unmeasured confounders.

This paper proposes a benchmark, expand, and calibration (BenchExCal) approach to trial emulation and describes the design and process for evaluating the performance of this approach through simulation studies and five planned empirical examples.

opinions.rationale: The claim is internally consistent and correctly scoped as a problem of current practice (lack of standardization and integration) rather than a structural impossibility. The reasons given for it being open (incompatible identification stories, untestable assumptions differing across tools) genuinely support the claim that these tools are not currently integrated into a standard emulation workflow. The severity is proportionate to the methodological gap.

title: Sensitivity analyses vary one violated assumption at a time when several are violated together
statement: A conventional emulation reports a point estimate under exchangeability, positivity and correct measurement, and then a sensitivity analysis that relaxes one of them. In a longitudinal emulation on routine data all of them are doubtful simultaneously: unmeasured confounding, selection into the cohort, misclassification of exposure and outcome, and practical positivity failure all operate at once and interact. There is little theory for the joint case, so the reported uncertainty is a sampling interval around a point that is identified only under a conjunction the analysis has already conceded is false. What is missing is a way to report an identification region reflecting all the violations together, separately from the sampling interval.
why_open: Bias parameters for different violations live on different scales and enter the estimating equations at different places, so there is no natural single-parameter family to sweep. The joint region is typically not a product of the marginal regions because the violations interact, which means the computationally convenient answer is also the wrong one. Reporting a wide identification region is also professionally costly: it makes an honest analysis look weaker than a naive one, and no journal currently requires it.

prior_work.cite: Hubbard RA, Hernán MA. "Target trial emulation" for observational studies: potential and pitfalls. N Engl J Med 2024
prior_work.what_it_does: Sets out the residual assumption burden that survives a correctly specified emulation, which is the set this problem asks to be handled jointly.

proposed_direction: Construct modular bias models whose parameters describe each violation separately, then obtain the joint uncertainty region by optimization over the parameter space or by Bayesian posterior sampling with priors on each bias parameter. Report the identification region and the sampling interval as two distinct objects, so a reader can see which part of the uncertainty more data would reduce. Establish, in simulation, how far the product of marginal sensitivity analyses misstates the joint region, since that is the approximation currently in use by default.
severity: Reported uncertainty systematically understates real uncertainty, in a direction that always favors the claim.

source.locator: seed-linked.md line 83, row 'Partial identification under multiple violations'

opinions.rationale: No work in the corpus reports a joint identification region over simultaneous unmeasured confounding, selection, misclassification and positivity failure in a longitudinal emulation, nor separates an identification region from a sampling interval in its reporting. Multiverse analysis of design choices is the nearest neighbor and varies design rather than bias parameters. The absence is consistent with the entry, and the confidence is capped because a partial-identification literature exists outside the eight search phrases used to build this corpus and would not have been retrieved.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Sensitivity analyses in longitudinal emulations vary one violated assumption at a time, and no reporting convention separates an identification region reflecting several simultaneous violations from the sampling interval.

opinions.rationale: Joint sensitivity analysis is a valid open workflow problem, but the statement treats possible threats as known simultaneous violations. Cohort selection is not necessarily bias for an estimand defined in that cohort, exposure or outcome misclassification need not be material, and practical near-positivity is an estimation problem rather than the structural nonpositivity that destroys identification. Performing a sensitivity analysis also does not concede that the identifying assumption is false. Interaction means one-at-a-time analyses generally cannot be combined mechanically; it does not imply that a Cartesian joint parameter space is always wrong. Without restrictions, simultaneous arbitrary confounding, selection, misclassification, and structural nonpositivity generally produce vacuous causal-effect bounds. A nontrivial identification region therefore requires explicit bounds and a coherent joint bias model. Bayesian sampling with priors on unidentified bias parameters yields a prior-sensitive posterior, not an identification region. More data can sometimes inform validation parameters or alleviate practical overlap problems, and omitted bias can point toward or away from a claim, so the asserted systematic understatement that always favors the claim is false. No R or Python package capability is asserted here.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Several material threats may coexist in a longitudinal routine-data emulation, and one-at-a-time sensitivity analyses need not characterize their joint effect. A joint analysis must specify compatible bias parameters, dependence restrictions, the target population, and the estimand, then distinguish the resulting partial-identification set from finite-sample uncertainty; without such restrictions, the causal-effect bounds may be vacuous.

opinions.rationale: The agenda claim that there is little theory for joint violations is not faithful. Multi-bias quantitative bias analysis is textbook material (Lash–Fox–Fink), with simultaneous adjustment methods, multiple-bias bounds, and released software. Smith, Mathur, and VanderWeele (2021) give composite bounds for unmeasured confounding, selection, and differential exposure/outcome misclassification and explicitly warn that one-at-a-time analysis can misstate joint impact. Brendel, Torres, and Arah (2023) develop simultaneous multi-bias adjustment via imputation and/or regression weighting for uncontrolled confounding, selection bias, and misclassification together; the CRAN package multibias (v1.7.3, still maintained 2026) implements that framework and advertises use for observational longitudinal real-world evidence. The EValue ecosystem documents multiple-bias bound examples. Gerlach-Wood et al. (2025) review QBA software and catalog tools that adjust several bias sources simultaneously (multibias, episensr variants, others), while still noting gaps and uneven simultaneous versus sequential implementations. For longitudinal time-varying treatment settings closer to sustained-strategy emulation, Tan (2025, Biometrika) formulates multi-period sensitivity models under sequential unmeasured confounding and contrasts joint versus product sensitivity models, which directly engages the report’s point that product-of-marginals can be the wrong answer. These works partially deliver the proposed direction: modular bias parameters, joint regions or adjusted estimates under several systematic errors, and (in probabilistic QBA) separation of systematic from sampling uncertainty. They do not fully close the problem as stated for a complete longitudinal g-methods target trial emulation in which unmeasured confounding, selection, measurement error, and practical positivity failure all enter one modular identification region reported as standard practice. Gao et al. (2025, Biometrics) still describe joint multi-assumption sensitivity for externally controlled trials as largely unexplored outside their omnibus contribution, which is useful counterweight to over-claiming full solution. No journal mandate for joint identification regions in TTE was found; professional cost of wide regions remains a social, not a mathematical, barrier. Package checks of TrialEmulation/gfoRmula/lmtp did not show native multi-bias identification-region reporting. So the correct status is partial solution of the joint multi-bias theory/software agenda for standard observational designs, with residual open work for full sustained-strategy TTE g-method modules and for ID-region-versus-sampling-interval reporting as a field norm. The claim of little joint theory is overstated relative to Smith–VanderWeele bounds, Brendel simultaneous multi-bias, multibias software, and Tan’s joint longitudinal sensitivity models.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Theory and software exist for joint multi-bias analysis of confounding, selection, and misclassification (and for some longitudinal sequential-confounding sensitivity models), but modular joint identification regions that also include practical positivity failure under sustained-strategy g-methods are not yet a standard, required part of target trial emulation reporting, and product-of-marginals approximations remain the default in practice.

resolving_work.title: Multiple-bias Sensitivity Analysis Using Bounds
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Gives a composite bound and sensitivity analysis for the joint impact of unmeasured confounding, selection bias, and differential exposure or outcome misclassification on a risk ratio, with explicit warning that one-at-a-time analysis can under- or over-state joint bias; implements the multiple-bias bound in the EValue tooling.
resolving_work.quote: By failing to consider multiple biases at once, researchers can underestimate—or overestimate—their joint impact. We show that it is possible to bound the total composite bias owing to these three sources and to use that bound to assess the sensitivity of a risk ratio to any combination of these biases.

resolving_work.title: Simultaneous adjustment of uncontrolled confounding, selection bias and misclassification in multiple-bias modelling
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Proposes simultaneous (not merely sequential) multi-bias adjustment for uncontrolled confounding, selection bias, and misclassification via imputation and/or regression weighting, evaluated as a joint alternative to one-bias-at-a-time analysis.
resolving_work.quote: A novel, alternative approach to multiple-bias adjustment involves the simultaneous adjustment of all biases via imputation and/or regression weighting.

resolving_work.title: multibias: Multiple Bias Analysis in Causal Inference (CRAN package)
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Released, maintained R software that simultaneously adjusts for any combination of uncontrolled confounding, exposure/outcome misclassification, and selection bias, based on Brendel et al. (2023), and marketed for observational longitudinal real-world evidence.
resolving_work.quote: The functions can simultaneously adjust for any combination of uncontrolled confounding, exposure/outcome misclassification, and selection bias. ... Simultaneous multi-bias analysis can be used to enhance the validity and transparency of real-world evidence obtained from observational, longitudinal studies. Based on the work from Paul Brendel, Aracelis Torres, and Onyebuchi Arah (2023) doi:10.1093/ije/dyad001.

resolving_work.title: Sensitivity models and bounds under sequential unmeasured confounding in longitudinal studies
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Develops multi-period sensitivity models and sharp/conservative bounds for longitudinal causal effects under sequential unmeasured confounding, and formulates joint versus product sensitivity models, addressing interaction of time-indexed assumption violations rather than a single one-at-a-time parameter.
resolving_work.quote: We consider sensitivity analysis for causal inference in a longitudinal study with time-varying treatments and covariates. ... joint and product sensitivity models

counter_evidence.quote: However, joint sensitivity analysis for multiple assumptions remains largely unexplored to the best of our knowledge.

opinions.rationale: The claim is internally consistent and correctly scoped as a gap in current practice and available theory rather than a structural impossibility. The reasons given for it being open (bias parameters living on different scales, non-product joint regions due to interactions, and professional costs) genuinely support the claim that joint sensitivity analyses are not standard and lack established, convenient theory. The severity is proportionate to the methodological gap.

evidence.quote: However, joint sensitivity analysis for multiple assumptions remains largely unexplored to the best of our knowledge.

dissent.rationale: The agenda claim that there is little theory for joint violations is not faithful. Multi-bias quantitative bias analysis is textbook material (Lash–Fox–Fink), with simultaneous adjustment methods, multiple-bias bounds, and released software. Smith, Mathur, and VanderWeele (2021) give composite bounds for unmeasured confounding, selection, and differential exposure/outcome misclassification and explicitly warn that one-at-a-time analysis can misstate joint impact. Brendel, Torres, and Arah (2023) develop simultaneous multi-bias adjustment via imputation and/or regression weighting for uncontrolled confounding, selection bias, and misclassification together; the CRAN package multibias (v1.7.3, still maintained 2026) implements that framework and advertises use for observational longitudinal real-world evidence. The EValue ecosystem documents multiple-bias bound examples. Gerlach-Wood et al. (2025) review QBA software and catalog tools that adjust several bias sources simultaneously (multibias, episensr variants, others), while still noting gaps and uneven simultaneous versus sequential implementations. For longitudinal time-varying treatment settings closer to sustained-strategy emulation, Tan (2025, Biometrika) formulates multi-period sensitivity models under sequential unmeasured confounding and contrasts joint versus product sensitivity models, which directly engages the report’s point that product-of-marginals can be the wrong answer. These works partially deliver the proposed direction: modular bias parameters, joint regions or adjusted estimates under several systematic errors, and (in probabilistic QBA) separation of systematic from sampling uncertainty. They do not fully close the problem as stated for a complete longitudinal g-methods target trial emulation in which unmeasured confounding, selection, measurement error, and practical positivity failure all enter one modular identification region reported as standard practice. Gao et al. (2025, Biometrics) still describe joint multi-assumption sensitivity for externally controlled trials as largely unexplored outside their omnibus contribution, which is useful counterweight to over-claiming full solution. No journal mandate for joint identification regions in TTE was found; professional cost of wide regions remains a social, not a mathematical, barrier. Package checks of TrialEmulation/gfoRmula/lmtp did not show native multi-bias identification-region reporting. So the correct status is partial solution of the joint multi-bias theory/software agenda for standard observational designs, with residual open work for full sustained-strategy TTE g-method modules and for ID-region-versus-sampling-interval reporting as a field norm. The claim of little joint theory is overstated relative to Smith–VanderWeele bounds, Brendel simultaneous multi-bias, multibias software, and Tan’s joint longitudinal sensitivity models.
